reviews.text: We are furious. Our 12-month-old Cavalier King Charles Spaniel had her ear cut off right at the beginning of her grooming session. The open wound was over 2 cm long. We had to rush her to the vet. The result: three stitches, a cone for two weeks, and part of her ear is damaged.

Walk-ins were welcome at the salon, and we were seen immediately—a huge plus for speed! In just an hour and a half, my dog ​​had a lovely muzzle trim, neatly trimmed paws, a complete hygiene check, and his belly shaved (we're letting his main coat grow back). Everything was done with great care and professionalism. We look clean and handsome. Thank you. The price is extremely reasonable: €65. I highly recommend this place.

My dog ​​Ziggy (a one-year-old Goldendoodle) was groomed here a week ago, and it was a very difficult experience, both for him and for my partner and me. I share this opinion because grooming should always be done with respect for the well-being of the animal and its owners.

Upon arrival, I felt pressured. I was told there was no alternative to shaving because of his matting, without any other options being considered or explained. The possible consequences of a very short shave (irritation, increased sensitivity to cold, skin discomfort, sometimes uneven regrowth) were not explained to me.

The environment was noisy, there were many people, and I could barely hear the groomer. I finally agreed, thinking that Ziggy would still keep some of his undercoat. I also felt guilty, even though I brush and comb him daily.

When I picked him up, I discovered he had been shaved completely bald. He had very uneven patches, bald spots behind both front paws, and visible redness. I received no explanation or real professional feedback on these issues, and the groomer wasn't there when he left. I was simply told that my dog ​​"lacked patience," even though he's usually gentle, cooperative, and used to being groomed. I tried not to show my distress to my dog ​​and to be cheerful because Ziggy is like a sponge, but inside I was devastated.

However, the most striking thing was his condition after the appointment. Ziggy has been showing unusual signs of distress for a week: restlessness, difficulty sleeping (he sat awake at the foot of the bed two nights in a row), hypervigilance, a constant need for reassuring contact, trembling, and extreme sensitivity to the cold, to the point that we had to buy him a sweater even though our house is well-heated. He had never exhibited this type of reaction before.

I understand that detangling can be difficult and that shaving is sometimes necessary, but I would have expected more explanation, transparency, and kindness, as well as a clean and skin-friendly result.

I also noticed that my dog's eyelashes and whiskers had been cut. These hairs are part of his sensory system and allow him to process various visual and olfactory stimuli; it is completely unacceptable to have them removed.

I returned to the shop a few days later to calmly share our experience. The groomer took the time to talk with us and seemed sorry, which I appreciated. However, I received no response from the other managers present that day, nor any compensation. €200 for an unwanted shave and the purchase of a coat made necessary by the situation is still hard to accept.
